hyperedges.label: Invoice to Reference to Collection Lifecycle

nodes.label: /add-endpoint Slash Command
nodes.rationale: Contract is updated first, then backend, then packages/core, then per-app UI, so an endpoint change lands as a single PR without contract/client/server drift.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY.md (Graphify setup guide)
nodes.rationale: Must run at the repo root, not inside backend/, because a backend-only graph misses the cross-language traversal (apps -> packages/core -> backend -> docs/api-contract.md) that is the whole reason to use graphify here. Never use `!` negation patterns in .graphifyignore: a single negation disables directory pruning and the scan descends into everything (graphify #882/#1276), causing monorepo-root scans to blow up to hundreds of MB.

nodes.label: SECURITY.md (credential rotation)
nodes.rationale: backend/auth.json has a neutral filename, so common secret-scanning tools do not flag it as sensitive; it must be explicitly listed in both .gitignore and .graphifyignore or it leaks quietly. Also warns never to distribute the template as a raw folder-zip since zipping ignores .gitignore and repacks vendor/, .env, and auth.json.

nodes.label: apps/_app-template/ui-kit.md (UI kit template doc)
nodes.rationale: The vendored kit is a read-only reference/resources provider, not the app skeleton: borrow and adapt only what a screen needs into the app's own lib/, never import the kit's Bloc/Cubit or package, to keep the app's own Riverpod/Dio/freezed architecture clean and deduplicated.

nodes.label: apps/pos/ui-kit.md (DevKit UI kit reference)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a read-only reference/resources provider: keep this app's own architecture (Riverpod, Dio, freezed), never import DevKit's Bloc/Cubit or package:devkit/..., and pull across only the assets a ported widget actually uses.

nodes.label: Laravel Best Practices Skill
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Consistency First: before applying any rule, check what the application already does; the best choice is the pattern the codebase already uses, even if theoretically suboptimal, because inconsistency is worse than a suboptimal pattern. These rules are defaults for when no pattern exists yet, not overrides.

nodes.label: addSelect() Subqueries for Single Has-Many Values
nodes.rationale: Eager-loading an entire has-many relationship just to read one value (e.g. latest timestamp/FK) wastes memory and queries; a correlated subquery via addSelect() pulls the value directly in the main SQL query with zero extra queries, and can be paired with a virtual belongsTo relationship for a fully-hydrated related model.
nodes.norm_label: addselect() subqueries for single has-many values

nodes.label: setRelation() to Prevent Circular N+1
nodes.rationale: When a parent is eager-loaded with children and the view also needs child->parent, letting Eloquent lazy-load the inverse relation fires N extra queries; injecting the already-loaded parent via setRelation() avoids the round trip entirely.

nodes.label: whereIn + Subquery Over whereHas
nodes.rationale: whereHas() emits a correlated EXISTS subquery that re-executes per row; whereIn() with a select('id') subquery lets the database use an index lookup instead, avoiding per-row re-execution and PHP memory overhead. Sometimes two simple, highly-selective queries beat one complex correlated query.

nodes.label: Compound Indexes Matching orderBy Order
nodes.rationale: Individual single-column indexes cannot combine for multi-column sorts; a compound index must match the ORDER BY column order or the database will filesort. Correlated subqueries in orderBy() avoid the row-duplication problem joins cause when sorting by a has-many value.

nodes.label: Single-Purpose Action Classes + Dependency Injection
nodes.rationale: Extracting discrete business operations into invokable Action classes with constructor-injected dependencies (avoiding app()/resolve()) and coding to interfaces at system boundaries (payment gateways, notification channels) improves testability and swappability.

nodes.label: defer() vs Queued Jobs for Post-Response Work
nodes.rationale: For lightweight, fire-and-forget tasks that don't need to survive a crash (logging, analytics, cleanup), defer() runs the callback after the HTTP response in the same process, avoiding queue overhead. Jobs are reserved for work that must survive process crashes or needs retry logic — an explicit trade-off between latency/simplicity and durability.
nodes.norm_label: defer() vs queued jobs for post-response work

nodes.label: Context Facade for Request-Scoped Data
nodes.rationale: The Context facade passes data through the entire request lifecycle (middleware, controllers, jobs, logs) without manual argument passing; it auto-propagates to queued jobs and log entries. addHidden() keeps sensitive data available to queued jobs while excluding it from logs; data that must not leave the process should not be stored in Context at all.

nodes.label: Concurrency::run() for Parallel Execution
nodes.rationale: Concurrency::run() executes independent closures in separate child processes with full Laravel access, avoiding the need for async libraries when running independent DB queries, API calls, or computations that would otherwise run sequentially.

nodes.label: Atomic Locks for Race Conditions
nodes.rationale: Cache::lock() or lockForUpdate() prevent race conditions where concurrent processes act on the same resource (e.g. order processing, stock decrement) without atomic protection.

nodes.label: mb_* String Functions for UTF-8 Safety
nodes.rationale: Standard PHP string functions (strlen, strtolower) count bytes not characters and silently corrupt multibyte text; mb_* functions are UTF-8 safe. Laravel's Str helpers (Str::length, Str::lower) are preferred over raw mb_* calls when available.
nodes.norm_label: mb_* string functions for utf-8 safety

nodes.label: $attributes->merge() in Component Templates
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding classes in a component prevents consumers from adding their own; merge() combines class attributes cleanly, preserving both the component's defaults and caller overrides.

nodes.label: View Composers for Shared View Data
nodes.rationale: If every controller rendering a given partial (e.g. a sidebar) must repeat the same data-passing code, that duplication should be centralized in a View Composer instead.
nodes.norm_label: view composers for shared view data

nodes.label: Blade Fragments for Partial Re-Renders
nodes.rationale: fragmentIf() lets a single view return either the full page or just a fragment based on the request (e.g. an HX-Request header), keeping htmx/Turbo routing clean without duplicating templates.

nodes.label: Cache::remember() Cache-Aside Pattern
nodes.rationale: Manual get/put cache-aside boilerplate is error-prone and repetitive; Cache::remember() encapsulates the check-then-compute-then-store pattern in one call.

nodes.label: Cache::flexible() Stale-While-Revalidate
nodes.rationale: On high-traffic keys, a strict TTL means one unlucky user always pays the full recompute cost when the cache expires. flexible() trades a little staleness for consistently fast responses by serving stale data while refreshing in the background.

nodes.label: Cache::memo() Per-Request Memoization
nodes.rationale: Reading the same cache key multiple times per request (e.g. a service called from several places) causes redundant round-trips to the cache store; memo() resolves the value once and reuses it in memory for the rest of the request.

nodes.label: Cache Tags for Group Invalidation
nodes.rationale: Without tags, invalidating a related group of cache entries requires tracking every individual key; tags let you flush atomically, at the cost of only working with redis/memcached/dynamodb, not file or database drivers.

nodes.label: Cache::lock() for Race Conditions
nodes.rationale: Referenced alongside remember() as the mechanism to serialize access when a race condition (rather than a stale-read) is the actual risk.

nodes.label: Higher-Order Messages for Simple Operations
nodes.rationale: $users->each->markAsVip() reads more directly than wrapping the same call in an explicit closure, for each/map/sum/filter/reject/contains and similar collection methods.

nodes.label: cursor() vs lazy() Trade-off
nodes.rationale: cursor() keeps only one model in memory at a time but silently ignores eager-loading, reintroducing N+1 risk if relationships are accessed; lazy() uses chunked offset pagination and does support eager loading. The choice depends on whether relationship access is needed.

nodes.label: lazyById() for Safe Mutation During Iteration
nodes.rationale: lazy()'s offset-based pagination can skip or double-process rows if records are updated mid-iteration; lazyById() uses id > last_id instead, which is safe against mutation.
nodes.norm_label: lazybyid() for safe mutation during iteration

nodes.label: toQuery() for Bulk Operations on Collections
nodes.rationale: Manually reconstructing a whereIn(pluck('id')) query to bulk-update a collection is boilerplate that toQuery() eliminates.
nodes.norm_label: toquery() for bulk operations on collections

nodes.label: env() Only in Config Files
nodes.rationale: Direct env() calls in application code silently return null once config is cached (php artisan config:cache), because cached config no longer reads the .env file; env() must be confined to config/*.php and accessed elsewhere via config().

nodes.label: Constants and Language Files Over Magic Strings
nodes.rationale: Magic strings for model states/types are error-prone to compare and refactor; class constants are preferred. Language files via __() should only be introduced when the app already uses them for localization — not retrofitted onto English-only apps, matching the Consistency First stance.
nodes.norm_label: constants and language files over magic strings

nodes.label: Eager Load Relationships to Prevent N+1
nodes.rationale: Lazy loading a relationship inside a loop issues one query per iteration (1+N queries); with() collapses this to a fixed small number of queries, and constraining the eager load's columns (always including the FK) further reduces payload.
nodes.norm_label: eager load relationships to prevent n+1

nodes.label: Model::preventLazyLoading() in Development
nodes.rationale: Enabling this in non-production throws LazyLoadingViolationException on any un-eager-loaded relationship access, surfacing N+1 bugs during development rather than in production.

nodes.label: chunk() / chunkById() for Large Datasets
nodes.rationale: Loading thousands of records via all()/get() risks memory exhaustion; chunk() batches results, but standard chunk() uses OFFSET which shifts if rows are modified mid-iteration — chunkById() must be used when modifying records during the loop.

nodes.label: withCount() Instead of Loading Full Relations to Count
nodes.rationale: Loading an entire has-many collection just to call ->count() wastes memory and bandwidth; withCount() computes the count in SQL, and conditional withCount clauses replace multiple separate count queries.
nodes.norm_label: withcount() instead of loading full relations to count

nodes.label: cursor() for Memory-Efficient Read-Only Iteration
nodes.rationale: cursor() streams one model at a time via a PHP generator for read-only iteration over large result sets; chunk()/chunkById() should be used instead when the iteration mutates records.

nodes.label: Add Database Indexes for WHERE/ORDER BY/JOIN Columns
nodes.rationale: Columns appearing in WHERE, ORDER BY, JOIN, and GROUP BY clauses need indexes; composite indexes should match common combined query patterns (e.g. WHERE status = ? ORDER BY created_at).
nodes.norm_label: add database indexes for where/order by/join columns

nodes.label: Local Scopes for Reusable Query Constraints
nodes.rationale: Duplicating the same where/whereNotNull constraints across multiple call sites (including inside whereHas closures) is error-prone; extracting a scopeXxx method makes the constraint reusable and named.
nodes.norm_label: local scopes for reusable query constraints

nodes.label: Apply Global Scopes Sparingly
nodes.rationale: A global scope silently modifies every query on the model, making debugging difficult and causing admin panels/reports/jobs to silently skip data (e.g. drafts); local scopes that callers opt into are safer except for truly universal constraints like soft deletes or multi-tenancy.

nodes.label: whereBelongsTo() Over Manual Foreign Key Queries
nodes.rationale: Manually specifying the foreign key column duplicates knowledge already encoded in the relationship definition; whereBelongsTo() is cleaner and relationship-aware.
nodes.norm_label: wherebelongsto() over manual foreign key queries

nodes.label: Avoid Hardcoded Table Names in Queries
nodes.rationale: String-literal table names in raw queries/joins/subqueries make it impossible to find all usages of a model and break refactoring when a table is renamed; (new Model)->getTable() keeps the reference traceable. Migrations are an explicit exception because they are frozen historical snapshots, not living references to a model that may later be renamed or deleted.
nodes.norm_label: avoid hardcoded table names in queries

nodes.label: Exception Reporting/Rendering: Co-located vs Centralized
nodes.rationale: Co-locating report()/render() on the exception class keeps behavior next to its definition and is easier to find; centralizing all handling in bootstrap/app.php gives one place to see the full picture. Both are valid — the existing codebase's established pattern should be followed rather than mixing the two.

nodes.label: ShouldntReport Interface
nodes.rationale: Implementing ShouldntReport on an exception class is more discoverable at the class definition than adding the class name to a dontReport() list buried elsewhere.

nodes.label: context() Method for Structured Exception Data
nodes.rationale: Attaching a context() method to an exception class lets Laravel automatically include structured data (e.g. order_id) in the log entry without manually threading it through every report() call.
nodes.norm_label: context() method for structured exception data

nodes.label: ShouldDispatchAfterCommit for Events
nodes.rationale: Without ShouldDispatchAfterCommit, a queued listener may run before the enclosing DB transaction commits, reading data that doesn't exist yet — a classic transaction-visibility race condition.

nodes.label: Always Queue Notifications
nodes.rationale: Notifications often call external APIs (email, SMS, Slack); without ShouldQueue they block the HTTP response, so notifications should implement ShouldQueue and route to dedicated queues per channel priority.

nodes.label: afterCommit() on Notifications in Transactions
nodes.rationale: Same transaction-visibility race as events: calling afterCommit() on the notify() dispatch delays it until the transaction commits.

nodes.label: Explicit timeout/connectTimeout on Every Request
nodes.rationale: The default 30s timeout is too long for most API calls; explicit timeout/connectTimeout make the client fail fast rather than hang, and service-specific macros centralize this configuration.

nodes.label: retry() with Backoff for External APIs
nodes.rationale: External APIs have transient failures; retry() with increasing delays avoids hammering a failing service, and retry predicates can restrict retries to specific error types (connection errors, 5xx) rather than all failures.
nodes.norm_label: retry() with backoff for external apis

nodes.label: Http::pool() for Concurrent Independent Requests
nodes.rationale: Sequential independent HTTP calls waste wall-clock time; Http::pool() issues them concurrently and lets each response be retrieved by name.

nodes.label: Http::fake() and preventStrayRequests() in Tests
nodes.rationale: Tests must never make real HTTP requests; Http::fake() with preventStrayRequests() guarantees this and lets both success and failure scenarios (failedConnection) be exercised deterministically.

nodes.label: ShouldQueue on Mailable Class
nodes.rationale: Implementing ShouldQueue on the mailable itself makes queueing the default regardless of call site, instead of relying on every caller to remember Mail::queue().

nodes.label: afterCommit() on Mailables in Transactions
nodes.rationale: A queued mailable dispatched inside a DB transaction may be processed before the transaction commits; calling $this->afterCommit() in the constructor delays sending until after commit.

nodes.label: assertQueued() Not assertSent() for Queued Mailables
nodes.rationale: Mail::assertSent() only catches synchronous mail; a ShouldQueue mailable fails that assertion with a hint to use assertQueued() instead — the two are not interchangeable.
nodes.norm_label: assertqueued() not assertsent() for queued mailables

nodes.label: Markdown Mailables for Transactional Email
nodes.rationale: Markdown mailables auto-generate both HTML and plain-text versions with responsive components and global style customization, reducing duplicated templating work.

nodes.label: Generate Migrations with Artisan
nodes.rationale: Manually created migration files risk wrong naming and missing timestamps that break migration ordering; php artisan make:migration guarantees consistent naming.

nodes.label: Never Modify Deployed Migrations
nodes.rationale: Once a migration has run in production it must be treated as immutable; further schema changes require a brand-new migration rather than editing history, or environments running the old migration diverge from ones running the edited version.

nodes.label: Add Indexes in the Migration, Not as an Afterthought
nodes.rationale: Indexes for WHERE/ORDER BY/JOIN columns should be declared at table-creation time in the migration, not retrofitted later, to avoid running production ALTER TABLE index-builds under load.
nodes.norm_label: add indexes in the migration, not as an afterthought

nodes.label: One Concern Per Migration (No Mixed DDL/DML)
nodes.rationale: Mixing schema creation and data insertion in one migration means a partial failure (e.g. the insert fails) can leave an unrecoverable state; separating DDL and DML into distinct migrations isolates failure modes. Reversible down() methods should be the default; intentionally irreversible migrations (destructive backfills) should be commented and paired with a forward-fix migration instead of a fake rollback.
nodes.norm_label: one concern per migration (no mixed ddl/dml)

nodes.label: retry_after Must Exceed Job timeout
nodes.rationale: If retry_after is shorter than a job's timeout, the queue worker re-dispatches the job while the original attempt is still running, causing duplicate execution of the same work.

nodes.label: Exponential Backoff for Job Retries
nodes.rationale: Fixed-interval retries can overwhelm a failing external service (e.g. Stripe); progressively longer delays ($backoff = [1,5,10]) give the dependency time to recover.

nodes.label: ShouldBeUnique / ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing
nodes.rationale: ShouldBeUnique prevents duplicate job processing by holding a lock until completion; ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing releases the lock as soon as processing starts instead, allowing new instances to queue sooner — a trade-off between strict de-duplication and throughput.

nodes.label: Always Implement failed()
nodes.rationale: Relying on silent failure hides job errors; implementing failed() lets the job update its own state and log the error explicitly. retryUntil() based time limits require $tries = 0 to avoid premature failure.

nodes.label: RateLimited Middleware for External API Calls in Jobs
nodes.rationale: Jobs calling third-party APIs should be throttled with RateLimited middleware to stay within the provider's rate limits.
nodes.norm_label: ratelimited middleware for external api calls in jobs

nodes.label: Bus::batch() for Related Jobs
nodes.rationale: Jobs that should succeed or fail together (e.g. CSV import chunks) belong in a Bus::batch() with then()/catch() callbacks, rather than being dispatched independently.

nodes.label: Implicit Route Model Binding
nodes.rationale: Manually resolving a model with findOrFail($id) duplicates what Laravel already does automatically from a typed route parameter.

nodes.label: Scoped Bindings for Nested Resources
nodes.rationale: scopeBindings() enforces that a nested resource actually belongs to its parent automatically, instead of requiring a manual check in the controller.

nodes.label: Keep Controllers Thin (Extract to Actions/Services)
nodes.rationale: Controller methods that mix validation, file handling, persistence, relation syncing, and event dispatch in one method (aim for under 10 lines) should have their business logic extracted into action or service classes.

nodes.label: Type-Hint Form Requests for Auto-Validation
nodes.rationale: Type-hinting a Form Request class triggers automatic validation and authorization before the controller method body executes, replacing inline $request->validate() calls.

nodes.label: withoutOverlapping() on Variable-Duration Tasks
nodes.rationale: Without it, a long-running scheduled task spawns a second overlapping instance at the next tick, causing double-processing or resource exhaustion.

nodes.label: onOneServer() on Multi-Server Deployments
nodes.rationale: Without onOneServer(), every server in a multi-server deployment runs the same scheduled task simultaneously; it requires a shared cache driver (Redis, database, Memcached) to coordinate.

nodes.label: Schedule Groups for Shared Configuration
nodes.rationale: Repeating the same chain of modifiers (onOneServer, timezone) across many scheduled commands is avoided by grouping them under one shared configuration.

nodes.label: Mass Assignment Protection ($fillable/$guarded)
nodes.rationale: $guarded = [] makes every model field mass-assignable from user input; every model accepting user input must whitelist via $fillable (or a deliberate $guarded) to prevent attacker-controlled fields being set.

nodes.label: Authorize Every Action via Policies/Gates
nodes.rationale: Updating/deleting a model without an authorization check lets any authenticated user act on any record; Gate::authorize() in the controller, or authorize() in the Form Request, must gate every mutating action.

nodes.label: Prevent SQL Injection via Parameter Binding
nodes.rationale: Interpolating user input directly into a raw SQL string is a classic injection vector; Eloquent/query builder parameter binding (or whereRaw with bindings) must always be used instead.
nodes.norm_label: prevent sql injection via parameter binding

nodes.label: Rate Limit Auth and API Routes
nodes.rationale: Authentication and API routes without a throttle middleware are vulnerable to brute-force and abuse; RateLimiter::for() plus the throttle middleware caps requests per identity (e.g. IP).
nodes.norm_label: rate limit auth and api routes

nodes.label: Keep Secrets Out of Code (config() Only)
nodes.rationale: env('API_KEY') calls scattered through application code bypass the config-cache-safe pattern; secrets must be defined once in config/services.php and read via config() everywhere else, with .env never committed.
nodes.norm_label: keep secrets out of code (config() only)

nodes.label: Laravel Naming Conventions Table
nodes.rationale: Consistent naming (singular controllers/models, plural snake_case tables, singular-alphabetical pivot tables, camelCase methods/variables) keeps the codebase predictable and matches Eloquent's own conventions (e.g. pivot table and FK auto-resolution rely on these conventions).

nodes.label: Prefer Str/Arr/Number/Uri Helpers Over Raw PHP
nodes.rationale: Raw PHP string/array functions (strtolower, str_replace, isset ternaries) are less readable and not always UTF-8 safe; Laravel's Str, Arr, Number, and Uri helpers are more chainable, readable, and safe, and should be preferred throughout.
nodes.norm_label: prefer str/arr/number/uri helpers over raw php

nodes.label: No Unnecessary Comments — Prefer Descriptive Names
nodes.rationale: A comment explaining what a conditional does is a signal the code itself isn't readable; extracting a well-named method (hasJoins()) replaces the comment entirely. Config files are the sole exception where comments are expected.
nodes.norm_label: no unnecessary comments — prefer descriptive names

nodes.label: LazilyRefreshDatabase Over RefreshDatabase
nodes.rationale: RefreshDatabase migrates once per process regardless of need; LazilyRefreshDatabase skips even that first migration when the schema is already current, speeding up the suite.

nodes.label: Call Event::fake() After Factory Setup
nodes.rationale: Model factories can rely on model events (e.g. a 'creating' event generating a UUID); faking events before the factory runs silences those events and produces broken models — Event::fake() must come after factory calls, not before.

nodes.label: Exceptions::fake() to Assert Exception Reporting
nodes.rationale: Instead of withoutExceptionHandling() which aborts the request, Exceptions::fake() lets the request complete normally while still asserting that the correct exception was reported.

nodes.label: Form Request Classes Over Inline Validation
nodes.rationale: Inline $request->validate() calls scatter validation logic across controllers; dedicated Form Request classes centralize both validation rules and (via authorize()) authorization for a given request.
nodes.norm_label: form request classes over inline validation

nodes.label: Array vs String Rule Notation
nodes.rationale: Array syntax composes more cleanly with Rule:: objects and is preferred for new code, but the project's existing Form Requests should be checked first and whatever notation is already established should be matched — an explicit restatement of the skill's Consistency First principle.

nodes.label: Always Use validated(), Never all()
nodes.rationale: $request->all() bypasses validation entirely for mass-assignment purposes, potentially persisting unvalidated or unauthorized fields; $request->validated() guarantees only checked fields are used.
